title: Delegation and Bounded Parallel Teams
summary: Kanban authority, workers, and isolated workspaces

lessons.title: Kanban authority
lessons.body: The Hermes Kanban board is canonical. Workers propose; controllers verify; only controller-owned dispatch mutates terminal state.

lessons.title: Bounded teams
lessons.body: Parallel workers get isolated worktrees and scoped toolsets; the supervisor watches progress, thrash, and budget.

lessons.title: Completion integrity
lessons.body: Completion is verified (deterministic criteria first, semantic second). Workers cannot self-complete.

lab.goal: Trace a task from creation to verified completion naming each authority boundary.
steps: In a sandbox, create a kanban task via the Hermes CLI.
Dispatch a worker and observe the supervisor diagnostics (nerve_work_event rows).
Attempt a worker self-completion and observe the controller-owned conversion.
lab.expect: You can draw the authority diagram from memory.

task.intro: Answer the scenario questions; the engine verifies them deterministically in a disposable fixture. Your answers are never executed as commands.

questions.q: May two workers own the same mutable artifact? (yes/no)
questions.why: No two workers may own the same mutable artifact.

questions.q: Name one isolation mechanism for parallel workers.
questions.why: Worktrees or separate isolated workspaces prevent shared-tree races.

questions.q: What must each delegated task end with? (evidence/none)
questions.why: Each task needs a tangible output plus a verification gate.

executable.task: Design a two-role team plan where no artifact has two owners.

check.question: Q: Who owns the final COMPLETE transition of a Kanban task?

troubleshooting: Worker-authored SQLite/CLI lifecycle mutation is fenced by the plugin.
Block submissions pass the deterministic block-review judge first.
